title: Class-group production release corpus
objective: Promote a bounded representative cubic class-group corpus into routine CI and add deterministic correctness, mutation, resource, and native/Wasm parity release gates against production sources

oracles: Committed Sage/PARI corpus records where an exact record identity is available
Production-source sealed-evidence replay plus ideal-certificate and projection mutation rejection

handoff.summary: Added a closed, versioned public-regression corpus and a dedicated qualification workflow. Pull requests replay five small cubics spanning trivial, cyclic, noncyclic, index-prime/nonmonogenic, and large-unit/regulator paths against exact discriminant, signature, equation-order index, class group, and unit-rank outputs. The test also checks conditional proof labeling, unconditional rejection, bounded relation exhaustion, recovery in a fresh process, authority-projection mutation rejection, and the existing exact ideal-certificate mutation replay. Row-6 is isolated in the scheduled/manual heavy profile and passed locally in 6.97 seconds. Optional native/Wasm parity runs automatically when the production reactor is present; absence is an explicit skip. The fixture states that all committed records are public regression data, not unseen evidence.
risks: The class-group product-service dependency is not yet complete, so the workflow currently builds the public qualification executable against packages/class-groups rather than invoking the final installed native service.
No production class-group Wasm reactor existed in this workspace, so the parity gate was inspected and explicitly skipped; it will become mandatory in the workflow once that artifact is built.
Only Linux x64 was executed in this lane. Linux arm64, macOS arm64, and the Windows Wasm fallback remain integration/release gates.

pnpm test:changed compared this long-lived integration branch with origin/main and selected thousands of unrelated files; it was stopped after merge:check passed rather than misrepresenting a repository-wide validation as lane-local evidence.

The branch-wide build reached its final numerical-Wasm stage but failed because the pre-existing numerical production manifest has a stale toolchain identity. After refreshing the runtime, pnpm test:portable passed 203 files including this corpus and then failed on the pre-existing modular q-expansion source freeze because architecture/package-graph.json changed elsewhere on the integration branch. Native and SEA lane gates were not run after those unrelated integration blockers, so the task remains active rather than falsely marked review-ready.
next_steps: Point SAGEJS_CLASS_GROUP_CORPUS_EXECUTABLE at the shipped product-service binary once class-group-product-service lands, without changing the corpus contract.
Build the production reactor before this test in the Wasm qualification job so the existing parity branch runs rather than skips.

Refresh the numerical production-manifest toolchain identity and the modular q-expansion source-freeze digest for the integration branch, then run pnpm test:portable, pnpm test:native, and pnpm test:sea and move this task to review.
Run the required cross-platform release matrix and sample genuinely unseen fields only after the candidate commit is frozen.
